minor.issue: subscription_service.get_subscription() unconditionally seeds `grace_until = _ROLLOUT_AT + 30d` on ANY newly-inserted non-admin subscription doc (line ~82). Docstring intent is 'existing paying customers pre-tier-rollout get grandfathered', but a user registering NOW (30d after rollout) is also flipped to `trader` tier via get_user_tier's `if state.get('in_grace'): return 'trader'` branch. Impact: brand-new users bypass all trader-level 402 gates (coach/broker-intel/replay-studio/evidence-board/vps_quick_connect/infra_pairing) for the first 30 days. Recommend gating grace on `user.created_at < _ROLLOUT_AT` (i.e. only pre-rollout users). Tests worked around this by clearing grace_until in the fresh-user fixture — see _force_starter() in test_iter120_tiered_subscriptions_http.py.

issues: Cosmetic only — 'Active: admin_grandfather · until 6/19/2036' banner exposes internal plan_id string to admin; could be prettified to 'Grandfathered access'. Not user-blocking.

action_items: OPTIONAL/LOW: In subscription_service.get_subscription, only seed grace_until when user.created_at < _ROLLOUT_AT (i.e. gate legacy grace on pre-rollout timestamp). Currently every new sign-up gets 30d trader-by-grace, silently bypassing trader-level 402 gates.
critical_code_review_comments: subscription_service.py:82 — `grace_until` is applied to every non-admin user regardless of created_at vs _ROLLOUT_AT. If the product intent is 'grandfather ONLY pre-existing customers', the seed should read `if user and not is_admin and user.get('created_at', now) < _ROLLOUT_AT`.

entitlements.enforce_feature/enforce_account_quota/enforce_mode_ceiling all fire before any payload validation on their host routes — good; means gate contract is stable regardless of body shape (verified against 12 endpoints in this run).

get_user_tier does not memoize inside a request — each gated route (potentially 4-6 on one page load like /subscription) will re-query db.subscriptions. Consider a per-request cache via Depends(...) or middleware for future iterations. Not urgent (Mongo hits are sub-ms) but visible in high-QPS use.
routes/subscription_routes.py:73 — /transactions returns `id: str(tx.get('_id') or '')` — correctly excludes raw ObjectId. Good pattern reused elsewhere.

routes/infra_routes.py:349 create_pairing wraps every non-ValueError/RuntimeError exception into 400 via `except Exception as e:` including the raw bson InvalidId message ('is not a valid ObjectId'). Fine, but consider a more user-friendly 'invalid account_id' message so the frontend upgrade-prompt modal doesn't have to string-sniff bson error text.
